about: Earlier passages a text assumes. Reading them first makes the passage easier to follow.

chain.label: Abraham meets Melchizedek
chain.note: A priest-king of Salem blesses Abraham, who gives him a tenth.

chain.label: A priest forever
chain.note: David's Lord is called a priest 'after the order of Melchizedek'.

chain.label: The Levitical priesthood
chain.note: The old priesthood Hebrews compares with Christ's.

chain.label: Abraham believed God
chain.note: 'He believed the Lord, and he reckoned it to him as righteousness.'

chain.label: The covenant of circumcision
chain.note: Paul asks whether Abraham was righteous before or after circumcision.

chain.label: David's blessing
chain.note: Paul uses David as a second witness to the blessing of forgiveness.

chain.label: The promise
chain.note: 'In you all the families of the earth will be blessed.'

chain.label: Faith counted as righteousness
chain.note: Paul's first proof text.

chain.label: The seed
chain.note: Paul reads 'seed' as singular, pointing to Christ.

chain.label: The manna
chain.note: The crowd cites the bread from heaven.

chain.label: A prophet like Moses
chain.note: The crowd wants to make Jesus a prophet-king after the feeding.

chain.label: Wisdom's banquet
chain.note: The invitation to eat the bread of wisdom.

chain.label: The Passover
chain.note: John notes that the Passover was near (6:4).

chain.label: The bronze serpent
chain.note: The people who looked at the raised serpent were healed.

chain.label: Hannah's song
chain.note: Mary's song echoes this prayer of a woman who was given a child.

chain.label: Promise to Abraham
chain.note: 'To Abraham and to his descendants for ever' (Luke 1:55).

chain.label: God's son out of Egypt
chain.note: Matthew applies Hosea's words about Israel to Jesus.

chain.label: Israel is my firstborn son
chain.note: Israel is called God's son in the Exodus.

chain.label: Jacob goes down to Egypt
chain.note: The first journey to Egypt, which sets up the Exodus.

chain.label: Man shall not live by bread alone
chain.note: Israel's forty years in the wilderness.

chain.label: Do not put the Lord to the test
chain.note: Israel's test at Massah (Exodus 17:1-7).

chain.label: Worship the Lord only
chain.note: The command of loyalty.

chain.label: Satan quotes the psalm
chain.note: The tempter's own use of Scripture.

entries.title: Jesus in the synagogue at Nazareth

chain.label: The anointed one
chain.note: The scroll Jesus reads.

chain.label: Let the oppressed go free
chain.note: Luke combines the two Isaiah passages.

chain.label: The widow and the leper
chain.note: Elijah and the widow of Zarephath.

chain.label: Naaman
chain.note: Elisha and the Syrian leper.

chain.label: The first sin
chain.note: The story Paul assumes.

chain.label: Death entered the world
chain.note: The warning.

chain.label: The one who was to come
chain.note: The promise of an offspring.

chain.label: Isaac and Ishmael
chain.note: Paul begins with those who are counted as the offspring.

chain.label: Jacob and Esau
chain.note: The choice 'before they were born'.

chain.label: Pharaoh
chain.note: The hardening and God's purpose.

chain.label: The potter
chain.note: The image behind Paul's potter.

chain.label: Crossing the sea
chain.note: The 'baptism into Moses'.

chain.label: Manna and the water from the rock
chain.note: The 'spiritual food and drink'.

chain.label: The golden calf
chain.note: 'The people sat down to eat and drink and rose up to play.'

chain.label: Apostasy at Peor
chain.note: The sexual immorality Paul mentions.

chain.label: The two sons
chain.note: Paul reads the story as an allegory.

chain.label: The barren woman
chain.note: 'Rejoice, O barren one.'

chain.label: Rebellion at Kadesh
chain.note: The generation that did not enter.

chain.label: Today if you hear his voice
chain.note: The psalm Hebrews quotes at length.

chain.label: The Sabbath rest
chain.note: God's own rest at creation.

chain.label: Abel, Enoch, Noah
chain.note: The first examples.

chain.label: Abraham and Sarah
chain.note: The central examples.

chain.label: Moses
chain.note: Moses' choice and the Passover.

chain.label: Rahab and the judges
chain.note: A string of examples ending in the prophets.

chain.label: The Suffering Servant
chain.note: The passage the official was reading.

chain.label: Every knee shall bow
chain.note: The text behind the hymn's close.

chain.label: The Servant
chain.note: The humility and exaltation pattern.

chain.label: The cry of abandonment
chain.note: The words Jesus speaks, which are also the start of a psalm that ends in praise.

chain.label: The Lion of Judah
chain.note: Jacob's blessing of Judah.

chain.label: The root of David
chain.note: The shoot from Jesse.

chain.label: The Son of Man
chain.note: The heavenly court scene.

chain.label: The scroll
chain.note: A scroll written on both sides.

chain.label: The offspring and the serpent
chain.note: The first enmity.

chain.label: Joseph's dream
chain.note: The sun, moon and stars.

chain.label: The dragon and the sea
chain.note: The beasts and the horns.

chain.label: A new heaven and a new earth
chain.note: The promise of a renewed creation.

chain.label: The river and the tree
chain.note: The river from the temple.

chain.label: Eden
chain.note: The first garden and the tree of life.

chain.label: In the beginning
chain.note: John echoes the first words of Scripture.

chain.label: Wisdom with God
chain.note: The figure who is with God at the creation.

chain.label: The glory of the Lord dwelt
chain.note: 'Grace and truth' echoes God's own name.

chain.label: A voice in the wilderness
chain.note: Mark's opening quotation.

chain.label: My messenger
chain.note: Mark attributes the combined quotation to Isaiah.

chain.label: Elijah
chain.note: John's clothing recalls Elijah.

chain.label: The commandments
chain.note: The text Jesus intensifies.

chain.label: An eye for an eye
chain.note: The case law Jesus reinterprets.

chain.label: Be holy
chain.note: The root of 'be perfect'.
